# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 21 (Bu-Vb Np21)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np21
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 21
**Title (English, from literature):** Keeping an extra almsbowl beyond ten days
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 21 (*Patta*) is the twenty-first rule in the forfeiture category of the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [Catalog]. The rule stipulates that a Buddhist monk who keeps an extra almsbowl for more than ten days commits an offense; he must relinquish the excess bowl and formally confess the transgression.

 Akira Hirakawa notes that in the parallel Mahāsāṃghika rule (NP 21), monastics are permitted only one bowl, and keeping excess bowls constitutes a violation [Hirakawa 1982].
